title: The Real Reason You Jolt With Fear When You Nearly Trip
hook: That sudden jolt when you almost trip is a primal reflex.

narration.text: That sudden jolt when you almost trip is a primal reflex.
It is called the startle reflex, and it happens incredibly fast.
Your brainstem, the most ancient part of your brain, takes over.
It bypasses the conscious thinking parts of your brain entirely.
This quick response prepares your body to either fight or flee.
It is why your heart races and muscles tense almost instantly.
This reflex keeps you safe from potential danger.
It is a vital survival mechanism, honed over millions of years.
Have you noticed this strong physical reaction in yourself?

description: Ever wondered why you get that sudden jolt of fear when you nearly trip? It is a fascinating brainstem response, an ancient survival mechanism that kicks in before you even have time to think. Discover the science behind this primal startle reflex.
topic: Why you feel a jolt of fear when you nearly trip or fall, explaining the startle reflex and brainstem response.
